findings.title: Any attendee can add guests to a booking
findings.body: The handler grants permission to any user whose email appears in `booking.attendees` via `isAttendee`. This exposes the tRPC mutation to every attendee, allowing them to add arbitrary emails to the booking without organizer approval. New attendees may receive calendar invitations and meeting details. Unless attendee self-service is an explicit requirement, restrict this mutation to the organizer or team admins/owners.

findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This means a team admin who is not an owner, or an owner who is not an admin, is denied. The variable name and intended behavior indicate an OR condition; use `||` or separate the two permission checks.

findings.title: Calendar update uses caller credentials instead of organizer's
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the authenticated caller's credentials, but the event belongs to `booking.user` (the organizer). The `EventManager` is then pointed at the organizer's destination calendar via `evt.destinationCalendar`. If the caller is not the organizer, this mismatch can make `updateCalendarAttendees` fail or attempt to update the wrong account's calendar. Use the booking organizer's credentials (e.g., `booking.user.credentials`) or load credentials for the organizer.

findings.title: Blacklisted email comparison is case-sensitive
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased before comparison, but incoming `guest` values are not normalized. An email such as `Blocked@example.com` can bypass a blacklist entry of `blocked@example.com` and be added to the booking. Normalize incoming guests with `.toLowerCase()` before comparing, or better normalize in the schema/handler before all validation.

findings.title: Incoming duplicate guests are not deduplicated server-side
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` filters incoming guests only against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist; it does not deduplicate the incoming `guests` array. The server schema `z.array(z.string().email())` does not enforce uniqueness, so a caller can pass the same email twice with different casing and `createMany` will insert duplicate attendee records for the same booking, causing duplicate calendar invites and inconsistent attendee data. Deduplicate case-insensitively on the server before insertion.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email disable settings
findings.body: Other email helpers in this file respect `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends organizer and attendee emails unconditionally. Users who disabled standard host or attendee emails for an event type will still receive these add-guests notifications, violating their email preferences. Pass `eventTypeMetadata` to this function and check the relevant disable flags before sending.

findings.title: No tests cover the new addGuests mutation
findings.body: This new tRPC mutation introduces authorization rules, email blacklisting, deduplication concerns, and external calendar/email side effects, but no tests are added. Missing coverage makes it easy for permission bypasses and duplicate-handling regressions to go unnoticed. Add tests for authorized and unauthorized callers, duplicate/blacklisted emails, and missing bookings.
